article.title: The Battle Over BAAJA and “Permitting Reform” Reinforces the Necessity of Expropriating Capital for Planetary Survival — The Black Alliance for Peace
article.content: “If one were forced for the sake of clarity to define [fascism] in a word, that word would be ‘reform.’” - George Jackson November 23, 2026 – Less than three weeks after the ‘Blue Wave,’ celebrated by the Democratic Party and its allies, U.S. Senate and House Democrats seem poised to join their Republican colleagues to advance the fascist, neoliberal march by passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). The bill sailed through the Senate with a significant number of Democrats, including current Minority Leader Schumer, joining the Republicans to secure its passage. The bill now moves to the House, where Republicans are working to fast-track it to President Trump’s desk for signature. Specifically, the bill makes major changes to environmental laws like the Clean Water Act and National Environmental Policy Act to speed up the development of energy projects. If enacted, it will erode environmental protections, land use regulations, and tribal sovereignty in a way that will devastate Black, Indigenous, and working-class communities, as well as the ecosystems they inhabit, under the guise of “permitting reform”. The Black Alliance for Peace denounces both the substance of the bill and the Democratic Party’s repudiation of the midterm elections’ popular rejection of the neoliberal status quo. Both aspects represent acts of economic, class, and environmental warfare against the working class; Black, Indigenous, and all oppressed peoples throughout the United States; and the planet. This bill – this “reform” – is not merely a question of environmental protections, but is rooted in domestic and global (neo)colonial usurpation of Indigenous sovereignty and the collective self-determination of the masses within the United States to achieve their People(s)-Centered Human Rights . It will further open the door for capitalist predation of oppressed and colonized peoples and communities throughout the United States, while reducing the already paltry legal avenues available to frontline communities and grassroots movements to oppose the destruction and poisoning of their lands, waters, and air. This comes at a time when the U.S. government and major technology companies are determined to continue the hyperscale data center buildout that is disproportionately being targeted at Black and Brown communities with little public input , and has already been accompanied by severe environmental deregulation in the past year . The battle against this specific bill has not been without resistance, particularly from Indigenous movements and communities over the attacks against tribal sovereignty and illegal land seizures that this bill would allow, as well as from movements against hyperscale data centers from across the country. However, what this bill and the battle around it reveal is that as long as the struggle for climate and environmental liberation is confined to legal determinations and fights against individual corporate or state projects, the masses are bound to lose. There can be no “just transition” or planetary survival with human dignity without the expropriation of capital, and continuing to live under the illusion that this class struggle can be avoided will only allow for the continued destabilization, disabling, and poisoning of our people and ecosystems. As BAP wrote this past April after the First Conference for Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels, “We maintain it is those peoples, nations, communities who paid the price that must define the solutions for a fossil-free future – against the greenwashing and liberal reformist tendencies that too often structure and dominate these conversations. There can be no climate and environmental justice without climate and environmental liberation, and there can be no path toward liberation that is not dedicated to fighting the interlocking systems of oppression that still shackle our people: imperialism, capitalism, (neo)colonialism, patriarchy, militarism, and white supremacy. This requires political clarity, concrete action, and sustained struggle…It is clear to BAP that while we must engage the institutions of power and decision-making ability, the only path forward from fossil fuel dependency and economy is the defeat of those interlocking systems of oppression through a unified, protracted struggle and social revolution based in People(s)-Centered Human Rights.” This task remains the same, and the necessity of coordinated anti-imperialist struggle against the capitalist system and the domination of fossil fuel and tech oligopoly, as well as the neocolonial political officials that serve them, is only more urgent. No Compromise, No Retreat.
